charts.name: 日本 参照勘定科目表（会社計算規則準拠）
charts.legal_reference: Japan prescribes no chart of accounts. 会社計算規則 (Ordinance on Company Accounting) prescribes the sections and the main items of the balance sheet of a 株式会社 (arts. 73 to 76) and of its income statement (arts. 88 to 94), and leaves every other subdivision to 'an appropriate name'. This chart is original: four digits by class — 1 assets, 2 liabilities, 3 net assets, 4 revenue and gains, 5 cost of sales, 6 selling and administrative expenses, 7 non-operating and extraordinary expenses, 8 income taxes — cut so that each range reaches one item of those articles, with the account names Japanese bookkeeping uses. No published chart, official or commercial, was copied. The books are kept tax-exclusive (税抜経理): the consumption tax collected sits on 仮受消費税等 and the tax paid on 仮払消費税等 until the return settles them.

numbering.legal_reference: 消費税法 art. 57-4(1) — a qualified invoice states the issuer's name and registration number, the date of the supply, what was supplied (saying which items are at the reduced rate), the total per rate with the rate, the 消費税額等 per rate, and the name of the recipient. No invoice number is among those particulars, which is why numbering is `free`; the pattern is one a business may choose.

payment_terms.legal_reference: No statute sets a payment term between businesses in general in the absence of an agreement, so legal_payment_days and late_payment_reference are empty. Terms imposed on certain subcontracting relationships by a separate act are not carried and were not read for this pack.

tax_point.legal_reference: 消費税法 art. 5(1) — a business owes the tax on the taxable supplies it has made, and art. 45(1)(i) — the return reports the supplies made during the taxable period: the tax follows the supply, not the invoice and not the payment. For goods that is the delivery, which is what `delivery_date` says; the Act's special rules for instalment sales, long-term construction contracts and a small business accounting on receipts (arts. 16 to 18) are not carried.

mentions.text: 輸出免税（消費税法第7条第1項）
mentions.legal_reference: 消費税法 art. 7(1) — the supply is exempt as an export; art. 57-4(1)(iv) asks the invoice for the total per rate, and the sentence says why no tax is charged on this line.

mentions.text: 非課税取引（消費税法第6条第1項・別表第二）
mentions.legal_reference: 消費税法 art. 6(1) and 別表第二 — the supply is non-taxable, so it is not a taxable supply and carries no 消費税額等 on a qualified invoice (art. 57-4(1) reaches only taxable supplies).

einvoicing.legal_reference: No Japanese statute obliges a business to issue or accept an electronic invoice. 消費税法 art. 57-4(5) lets a qualified invoice issuer provide the particulars of a qualified invoice as an electromagnetic record instead of paper, which is what a Peppol invoice is. The Digital Agency is the Japan Peppol Authority and maintains JP PINT, the Japanese specification of the Peppol International model (Peppol BIS Standard Invoice JP PINT 1.1.3, customization urn:peppol:pint:billing-1@jp-1). Its tax categories are S (standard), AA (lower rate), E, G and O. A party is addressed by its 法人番号 (corporate number, EAS 0188), as the JP PINT examples show, and the seller's tax registration identifier is the registration number of the qualified invoice issuer (EAS 0221), which the NTA's register publishes as T followed by thirteen digits. JP PINT asks the tax per rate to be rounded to the yen, between the floor and the ceiling, and leaves the direction to the issuer.
